greeting: In Jesus’ name, we gather in the sign of the Cross: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who sets us free, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.
Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed be the name of the Lord forever.
homily:
We often think of freedom as the ability to do whatever we want, whenever we want. We think of it as a blank map, a wide-open horizon where no one tells us 'no' and no one sets a boundary. But today, Saint Paul speaks of a different kind of freedom. He speaks of the Jerusalem above, the 'freeborn woman' who is our mother. He reminds us that we are not children of slavery, but children of the promise. Think for a moment of a child running toward their father. They aren't running away from something; they are running toward someone. That is true freedom. It is the liberty to belong, the safety of being known, and the courage to be exactly who God created you to be.

Benjamin Vo understood this kind of freedom. He was a boy who moved through the world with a rare, unhurried grace. Think of that image of Ben, perhaps on one of those summer trips, sitting cross-legged in a peaceful meditation pose in front of a grand, ornate temple. He wasn't just sitting there; he was present to the moment. He was a boy who looked at the world with a gaze of pure wonder. He didn't need to dominate the space; he simply enjoyed the beauty of it. He had a brilliant, analytical mind—the kind that could map out complex business ideas or code games in his GitHub repository with the precision of a master—but he never let that brilliance turn into pride. His brilliance was always tempered by a gentle, giggling joy. When he talked about his dream of 'con chim airlines,' he wasn't just talking about airplanes; he was talking about the joy of flight, the beauty of the sky, and the simple, innocent pleasure of imagining a world where everything could soar.

There is an ache in this, I know. I speak to you, Alan and Thao, and to you, Ryan. I know that the silence in your home can sometimes feel like a weight. You look for that giggle, you look for that bright, curious face, and the world feels smaller without him. You might wonder if you are doing enough, if you are 'getting it right' as you walk this path of grief. You might even feel a flicker of guilt, wondering if you missed a sign or could have steered things differently. Let me tell you this, as clearly as I can: you are not under a yoke of slavery. You are not bound by the 'what ifs' or the 'should haves.' God does not hold your heart to a standard of perfection; He holds your heart in His mercy. You were the parents Ben needed. You were the brother he adored. That bond is not a chain; it is a grace. It is a promise that, just as Ben was free to love you, you are free to be loved by God, even in the middle of your tears.

In the Gospel today, Jesus speaks of the sign of Jonah. People were looking for something spectacular, something that would force them to believe. But Jesus points them back to the simple, humble reality of a prophet who was sent to Nineveh. He points them to a truth that is 'greater than Solomon' and 'greater than Jonah.' He points them to Himself. Sometimes, we look for signs in our own lives. We look for a reason for the things we cannot understand. We look for a logic that explains why a life so full of promise, like Benjamin’s, seems to end before the story feels complete. But the Gospel tells us that the sign is not a puzzle to be solved; the sign is a Person to be followed. The sign is the love of God, which is present even when the world feels dark.

Think of the way Ben lived. He didn't wait for a sign to be kind. He didn't need a reason to be generous. Remember that moment when he, at only fifteen, offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle? He didn't need to break the bank, he didn't need to make a spectacle of it; he simply offered. That was his heart. That was his freedom. He was already a child of the promise. He lived with an open hand because he knew, in that gentle, intuitive way of his, that everything we have is a gift from the Father. He was free because he wasn't trying to hold onto anything too tightly.

Ryan, my brother, you are the keeper of those memories—the road trips, the snacks, the laughter. You are the one who knows the rhythm of his heart. When you feel the weight of his absence, don't try to carry it alone. You don't have to be 'strong' in the way the world demands. You just have to be yourself, the brother Ben loved. You are free to miss him, free to cry, and free to laugh at the memories you shared. That is the freedom of the children of God. You are not a slave to your grief; you are a son of the promise, just as Ben is a son of the promise. He is not gone; he is simply at the destination he was always meant for.

To all of you who are tuning in from afar, carrying your own heavy crosses, know this: you are seen. Whether you are a parent who has lost a child, or a person who feels overwhelmed by the pressures of life, you are not forgotten. The Lord, who raised the lowly from the dust, is the same Lord who is holding your hand today. Do not let the 'yoke of slavery'—the fear, the regret, the feeling that you are not enough—take root in your heart. You are free. You are free to be weak, free to be sad, and free to be held by the One who loves you more than you can imagine.

So, what can you carry out the door today? It is a small, quiet thing. The next time you see a bird or look up at the sky and see a plane tracing a line through the clouds, take a breath and whisper, 'Thank you.' Thank you for the gift of Benjamin. Thank you for the promise of the Jerusalem above. Thank you that we are not alone. And then, do one small thing that Ben would have done—share a giggle, offer a kind word, or just sit quietly for a moment and appreciate the beauty of the world. Ben’s life was a light that didn't just flicker; it burned bright, and it continues to burn in the hearts of everyone who knew him. He is safe. He is free. And he is waiting for you at the end of the journey, where the flight is smooth and the joy is endless.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you always. Go in the freedom of the children of God. Amen.
standing_petitions: For Benjamin Vo and all who have died, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace.
For all who grieve, especially Alan, Thao, and Ryan, that God may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text: Brothers and sisters: It is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the freeborn woman. The son of the slave woman was born naturally, the son of the freeborn through a promise. Now this is an allegory. These women represent two covenants. One was from Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery; this is Hagar. But the Jerusalem above is freeborn, and she is our mother. For it is written: Rejoice, you barren one who bore no children; break forth and shout, you who were not in labor; for more numerous are the children of the deserted one than of her who has a husband. Therefore, brothers and sisters, we are children not of the slave woman but of the freeborn woman. For freedom Christ set us free; so stand firm and do not submit again to the yoke of slavery.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text: R. Blessed be the name of the Lord forever. Praise, you servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD. Blessed be the name of the LORD both now and forever. R. Blessed be the name of the Lord forever. From the rising to the setting of the sun is the name of the LORD to be praised. High above all nations is the LORD; above the heavens is his glory. R. Blessed be the name of the Lord forever. Who is like the LORD, our God, who looks upon the heavens and the earth below? He raises up the lowly from the dust; from the dunghill he lifts up the poor. R. Blessed be the name of the Lord forever.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: While still more people gathered in the crowd, Jesus said to them, “This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, but no sign will be given it, except the sign of Jonah. Just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will the Son of Man be to this generation. At the judgment the queen of the south will rise with the men of this generation and she will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and there is something greater than Solomon here. At the judgment the men of Nineveh will arise with this generation and condemn it, because at the preaching of Jonah they repented, and there is something greater than Jonah here.”

day: Monday of the Twenty-eighth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
